sections.body: Course design and teaching is where AI helps instructors build curricula, write assessments, adapt materials, and support students. In practice, AI systems map topics to learning outcomes, draft quiz questions, summarize readings, and generate lecture slides from notes. They can also flag students who may need help by analyzing engagement and performance data. The work is not about replacing teachers, it is about reducing repetitive preparation and giving more feedback loops. These tools operate on course documents, syllabi, past exams, and student interaction logs. The field asks how to keep human judgment in the loop while scaling routine tasks.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are solved well enough for daily use, such as generating multiple choice questions from a textbook chapter or turning bullet notes into a slide outline. Curriculum mapping is harder because it depends on institutional context, accreditation rules, and tacit knowledge. Personalised learning and early warning systems can identify patterns, but they often struggle with false positives and with explaining why a student is flagged. Course-specific tutors can answer questions about a syllabus, yet they may hallucinate policies or invent deadlines if not grounded in the actual course materials. The honest limits include data privacy, bias in predictions, and the difficulty of measuring whether learning actually improved. The site's library holds 135 research papers, which shows the evidence base is growing but still uneven across these tasks.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The page on Curriculum and Learning Outcomes covers how AI helps align topics, skills, and assessments to formal goals. Generating Assessments focuses on creating questions, rubrics, and feedback drafts from course content. Personalised Learning and Early Warning looks at adaptive paths and risk detection, including the ethical questions around monitoring students. Course-Specific AI Tutors deals with chatbots and assistants trained on a single syllabus or set of lecture notes. Lecture Materials from Notes addresses the pipeline from raw notes to slides, handouts, and study guides. Together these pages move from planning, to assessment, to student support, to delivery materials, and a reader can start with the page that matches their immediate teaching task.
